The target video is a retro screen-print collage pop-art animation with a pink, black and white palette, halftone dot textures, paper grain and beat-synced cuts at about 110 BPM.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>: the full poster, centered and filling the frame, fades in from black as the a cappella vocal begins. The halftone dots across the pink background pulse gently with each vocal syllable, and the small black star near the top-left corner floats up half a centimeter and settles. The camera pushes in toward the poster's center with small amplitude at slow speed. The texts "weird-girl" and "STRANGE GIRLS CLUB" remain static.
[Shot 2] At 00:04.242, the shot cuts through a graphic match on a cluster of halftone dots that grows into an extreme close-up of <Subject 1>'s face, her dark hair with straight bangs and dark eyes framed by pink paper. Her eyes blink once on the first downbeat; the "weird-girl" text at the left edge of the frame shivers subtly with the vocal. The camera holds a static close-up with a very slow push-in.
[Shot 3] At 00:08.483, the shot pulls back to a wider view: the star, the heart and the globe from <Subject 2> lift off the poster surface one after another and float in shallow 3D space around <Subject 1>, casting soft halftone shadows. Her expression shifts from neutral to a small confident smirk, and her head tilts two degrees to the right. The camera trucks right at slow speed with small amplitude, keeping the floating symbols layered in front of the pink paper. The segment ends on this composition, cut cleanly on the beat.
